key_insight: Anatomically realistic physical CT phantoms can standardize site-specific testing and ongoing monitoring of AI performance.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help hospitals verify that CT-based AI tools remain reliable on their local scanners and workflows before and during use.
method: Built physical phantoms matched to the AI model’s expected anatomical input.
Tested AI performance across two clinical CT systems while varying scanner technology and operating conditions.
Tracked performance longitudinally over 15 months and checked whether phantom-trained models generalized to patients.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent longitudinal results over 15 months on both systems and effective generalization from phantom-trained models to patient data.
watch_item: Phantom-based testing may not capture every real-world clinical variation, so local validation still needs to be complemented by patient-centered evaluation.
paper_title: Standardised evaluation and monitoring of site-specific AI performance with physical CT phantoms
